requirement: Separate validators can verify the same source node and criterion concurrently on the same domain. Each execution has its own dependency trace and agent conversation. Each validator counts only its own executions.
rationale:
The two marked tests cover each obligation in `requirements.sdk.graph.running-criteria.verify.concurrent`.

**Concurrent verification of the same node and criterion on one domain.**
- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/tests.rs#fn[agent_executions_isolate_conversations_and_dependency_traces]` runs two separate `validation::Validator`s on one `Memory` graph. Both verify the same subject `Node(1)` and have equal `criterion_path()` and `source_node_id()`. They run under `futures::join!` with a 2s timeout. The provider in `impl[ParallelConversations/CompletionProvider]` awaits a 2-party `Barrier` every turn, so the executions must really overlap or the test times out.
- `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/contracts.rs#fn[concurrent_same_criterion_executions_keep_complete_independent_records]` verifies the same criterion `["behavior"]` from two validators on one `Application` domain. Both executions meet at a shared barrier, with the message "same-criterion executions must not wait for each other". It asserts each output (`first` and `second`).

**Each execution has its own agent conversation.**
- `ParallelConversations` requires `chat_history[0]` to be the system message `alpha` or `beta`.
- It asserts the history length grows by exactly 2 per turn.
- It asserts the serialized history contains only its own content and never the other conversation's content (`ALPHA-CONTENTS` or `BETA-CONTENTS`).
- It checks that the last delivered page belongs to the same conversation. Both conversations deliberately use the same tool-call ID (`same-call-id`), so a mix-up through that ID would be caught.
- The test also asserts per-prompt call counts of 3 each, and the final outputs `alpha` and `beta`.

**Each execution has its own dependency trace.**
- In the agent test, alpha's stored record has dependencies exactly `[Node(1)]`. Beta's record has exactly `[OutgoingEdges(Node(1), …), Node(2)]`. Each is loaded after its own `store_evidence`.
- The contracts test's `Review` executions read different nodes (`Node(2)` and `Node(3)`), and each has its own revision.
- Only one record survives in that test, so it checks only the surviving record's dependencies, and only against its own input. Together with the agent test, which checks both traces, this is sufficient.
- The contracts test also asserts `executions == 2`, `writes == 2` and `records.len() == 1`. Nothing is stored before `store_evidence`.

**Each validator counts only its own executions.**
- Each validator reports `usage().attempts == 3`, and the shared cache reports 6.
- Tool usage is checked per validator. Each of `read_node`, `get_next_page` and `submit_result` has 1 call per validator and 2 in the cache total. The cache's `result_bytes` equals the sum of the two validators' bytes. The initial usage was empty.

No obligation in the subject text is untested, and no `{fixme}` acknowledgments apply.
